findings.reason: §4 must still name `DEFAULT_INDEX_PATH` (`watch.py:91`) as the declaration it replaces and add `watch.py:1306`, `:1433` and the three CLI help strings to its write scope, or the new resolver is a fourth statement of a fact already written in five places and the GPFS path stays reachable through the reader's own fallback.
findings.text: the plan's new resolver `imas_ambix/agent/index_placement.py` (§4) is the fourth declaration of the same fact; `DEFAULT_INDEX_PATH` is already the owner and is duplicated at `imas_ambix/agent/watch.py:1306` and `:1433` (`Path(index_path or DEFAULT_INDEX_PATH)`), in three CLI option help strings at `imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:3096`, `:3197` and `:3292`, and in a second argparse entry point at `imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_ingest.py:486` whose own `TelemetryIndex(args.index_path)` at `:527` opens the index without passing through `cli.py` at all; its `--index` is `required=True`, so it cannot silently resolve the GPFS path, and the fleet service runs the CLI form instead (`services.json`: `agent ingest --cadence 60`, no `--index-path`, landing on `DEFAULT_INDEX_PATH` at `imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:3380`), which §4's write scope does cover

findings.reason: without the sentence naming the file-level hour tier as distinct (it is per-file and per-counter-total, not per-measurement-hour with gauge integrals) a reviewer cannot tell whether §5 is a second rollup over the same data, and the plan cannot be judged against `f-srw-020`'s own scope; the plan should state the distinct axis (`(host, boot_id, inode), measurement, hour`) and cite the tiers it does not replace.
findings.text: §5 introduces an hourly rollup and a name/kind dictionary as a new index-internal mechanism without citing the rollup machinery the codebase already has; `imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_store.py:1` owns three compaction tiers (raw/minute/hour) per receipt file and `telemetry_index.py:83`-:90 already exploits them by reading only the finest tier offered for a job (raw, else minute, else hour), and `receipt_bins` is named in the same docstring as the owner of receipt aggregation — the plan states the rollout "takes over f-srw-020 unchanged" but never states why the existing hour tier cannot answer a period read, and the `measurement` table's `measurement_lookup` index at `telemetry_index.py:277` already carries `(name, kind, sample_id)`

findings.reason: a second implementation of the atomic-publish contract is a second place for `published_at`/`compute_seconds`/mode 0644 to drift, and the honest change is to extract the body of `one_iteration` and call it from both call sites.
findings.text: §6 folds publication into the ingest's `on_tick` hook and restates its contract ("`published_at` and `compute_seconds` at top level, mode 0644, one flushed line per publication, and a failed publication leaving the previous file byte-identical") without naming `one_iteration`, which already implements exactly that contract (atomic temp-file write through `os.replace`, the two fields, one flushed line, one iteration) and is reached today through the `publish-watch` loop; the plan should call that function rather than re-implement its behaviour inside the hook

findings.reason: the plan should say the index is captured by the `on_tick` closure, or widen the hook; as written the interface between the loop and its two new responsibilities is undeclared, which is precisely where a spread of shallow wrappers accumulates.
findings.text: §4 and §6 both wire new work through `on_tick: Callable[[TickReport], None] | None`, whose parameter carries only a `TickReport`; the daily snapshot (§4) and the publication (§6) each need the index handle or its connection, neither of which the hook supplies, so the plan's claim that "`telemetry_ingest.py is not touched" is true only because a closure defined in `cli.py` reaches the index out of band, and it leaves the hook's declared type still describing a callback that can no longer do what the loop must

findings.reason: §4's resolver also has a merge available it does not claim (`DEFAULT_INDEX_PATH`, and §7's log-directory resolution sits beside the same environment-variable family), so the section should either name that retirement or state why the excluded artefact cannot be delegated.
findings.text: with the week's budget at `public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0`, §4 adds a new module whose public surface is a resolver, a journal-mode setter and its refusal on a network filesystem, so it adds to `public_definitions` and to `refusal_families` (the `statfs`-network-type refusal, `index_placement.py` in §4's own write scope), and §7 adds `$AMBIX_LOG_DIR` as a new configuration surface beside the existing `AMBIX_AGENT_ENGINE_ENV_ROOT` / `AMBIX_AGENT_ENGINE_ENV_MIN_FREE_GB` in `imas_ambix/agent/AGENTS.md` §3; the section names no definition it retires or merges and no reason none can be, unlike §6 which at least states that `publish-watch` "loses its loop" and so narrows the interface to one standing process

findings.reason: the two own different artefacts (machine geometry bundles versus the telemetry index) and neither cache root is a general-purpose one another can extend without widening its purpose, so the honest reading is a shared shape rather than a duplicated owner; naming it in §4 would still help a reader see the precedent.
findings.text: §4 rebuilds, for the index, a resolver shape this repository already has: an environment override, a durable shared root and a node-local staging root, in a stated resolution order (`durable_cache_root` at `:256`, `staging_cache_root` at `:271`, "In order: the environment override, the durable cache root, the node-local staging root, and finally re-authoring it"); the plan's three-case order is the same idea over a different artefact, and `artifact_resolution.py` is named as the owner of cache-root placement by its own importers (`imas_ambix/gs/machine_selection.py:46`, `imas_ambix/spine_bench/machine_artifact_arm.py:64`)

findings.reason: this is an observation about the plan's own account of itself, not a defect; §3 already reads as an in-place extension and needs no change, and §5's finding above is where the change belongs.
findings.text: the plan's own best reuse case is not cited as such: §3 does not add machinery at all, it changes the existing read path in place (`_read_new`, `_was_rewritten`, `_digest_of`, `prefix_sha` at `imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:1444` and `:1804`), which is exactly the "extend the mechanism" outcome this rubric asks for, and the plan's §5 by contrast adds a table and a dictionary

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `index_placement.py` hides path resolution, the WAL/journal-mode refusal, snapshot, retention and restore behind one small surface; that is depth, not a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — index path resolution is owned today by `imas_ambix/agent/watch.py:91`, declared in three CLI help strings and re-declared in a second argparse entry point; the plan adds a fourth resolver and omits the owner from its write scope.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 adds a resolver and its refusal family and §7 adds `$AMBIX_LOG_DIR`, and neither section names anything it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 extends the existing read path in place (good), but §4 and §5 add machinery without naming the owners they supersede: `DEFAULT_INDEX_PATH` for index placement and the existing minute/hour tiers for rollups.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §6 re-implements atomic publication inside the ingest tick and §4 adds a second index entry point, both beside existing machinery that already does the job.
